cve_summary: net/ceph/auth_x.c in Ceph, as used in the Linux kernel before 3.16.3, does not properly validate auth replies, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted data from the IP address of a Ceph Monitor.
commit_message:
libceph: do not hard code max auth ticket len

We hard code cephx auth ticket buffer size to 256 bytes.  This isn't
enough for any moderate setups and, in case tickets themselves are not
encrypted, leads to buffer overflows (ceph_x_decrypt() errors out, but
ceph_decode_copy() doesn't - it's just a memcpy() wrapper).  Since the
buffer is allocated dynamically anyway, allocated it a bit later, at
the point where we know how much is going to be needed.

Fixes: http://tracker.ceph.com/issues/8979

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ilya Dryomov <ilya.dryomov@inktank.com>
Reviewed-by: Sage Weil <sage@redhat.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Processes a single ticket for the Ceph authentication client, handling decryption and updating session keys.

Parameters: 
ac (struct ceph_auth_client*): Pointer to the Ceph authentication client structure.
secret (struct ceph_crypto_key*): Pointer to the cryptographic key used for decryption.
p (void**): Pointer to the data buffer containing the ticket information.
end (void*): Pointer to the end of the data buffer.

Returns: 
int: Returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: 
The function begins by decoding the ticket type and structure version. It retrieves the appropriate ticket handler and decrypts the ticket data. It then updates the session key and validity information based on the decrypted data. If the ticket is encrypted, it decrypts it using the old session key; otherwise, it directly copies the data. The function finally updates the ticket blob and validity parameters in the ticket handler, cleans up allocated resources, and returns the result of the operation.
"""
